facts.fact: Under the Modified Interest Subvention Scheme (MISS) for FY 2025-26, the lending rate to farmers is 7% a year
facts.quote: The applicable lending rate to farmers and the rate of interest subvention for the financial year 2025-26 will be as follows: Financial Year Lending rate to farmers Rate of Interest Subvention to Lending Institutions 7% 1.50% 2025-26

facts.fact: The Government pays lending institutions 1.5% interest subvention
facts.quote: Farmers received short-term loans of up to Rs.3 lakh through Kisan Credit Cards (KCC) at a subsidized interest rate of 7% , with 1.5% interest subvention provided to eligible lending institutions.

facts.fact: Farmers who repay on time get an extra 3% a year interest subvention (Prompt Repayment Incentive)
facts.quote: (ii) An additional interest subvention of 3% per annum will be provided to such of those farmers repaying in time

facts.fact: Farmers who repay on time therefore pay an effective 4% a year
facts.quote: This also implies that the farmers repaying promptly as above would get short term crop loans and/or short term loans for allied activities including animal husbandry, dairy, fisheries, bee keeping etc. @ 4% per annum during the financial year 2025-26.

facts.fact: Timely repayment means by the due date fixed by the bank, subject to a maximum of one year from disbursement
facts.quote: upto the due date fixed by the banks for repayment of such loan/s, whichever is earlier, subject to a maximum period of one year from the date of disbursement.

facts.fact: Farmers who repay after one year do not get the Prompt Repayment Incentive
facts.quote: This benefit would not accrue to those farmers who repay their agri loans after one year of availing such loans.

facts.fact: Official sources differ on the MISS limit: RBI's MISS circular for FY 2025-26 (13 Jan 2026) applies interest subvention and the Prompt Repayment Incentive up to an overall Rs 3 lakh a year, while PIB (Ministry of Agriculture) says the crop loan limit under MISS was raised from Rs 3 lakh to Rs 5 lakh in 2025-26
facts.quote: Interest subvention and prompt repayment incentive benefits on short term crop loans and short term loans for allied activities will be available on an overall limit of ₹3 lakh per annum
facts.note: PIB backgrounders (11 Mar 2026, 16 Jul 2026) repeat the Budget 2025-26 announcement that the MISS limit was raised to Rs 5 lakh, but the operative RBI MISS circular of 13 Jan 2026 keeps Rs 3 lakh; the expected answer already treats Rs 5 lakh as not to be stated without qualification. Coordinator 28 Oct: made a conflict so a bot citing either official page is not marked wrong; the same PIB release also says 'Short-term agri-loans up to Rs 3 lakh are available at 7% interest'.
facts.was: MISS benefits apply up to an overall limit of Rs 3 lakh (no other figure accepted)

also.quote: the crop loan limit under MISS, which has been raised from Rs 3 lakh to Rs 5 lakh.

facts.fact: Farmers engaged only in allied activities (animal husbandry, dairy, fisheries, bee-keeping) have a sub-limit of Rs 2 lakh
facts.quote: subject to a maximum sub-limit of ₹2 lakh per farmer in respect of those farmers involved only in activities related to animal husbandry, dairy, fisheries, bee keeping etc.

facts.fact: The crop-loan component takes priority for the subvention benefits; the rest goes to allied activities
facts.quote: The limit for crop loan component will take priority for interest subvention and prompt repayment incentive benefits and the residual amount will be considered towards allied activities

facts.fact: The latest notified MISS guidelines are for FY 2025-26
facts.quote: Government of India has approved the continuation of the Modified Interest Subvention Scheme (MISS) for the financial year 2025-26 with the following stipulations
facts.note: Searched rbi.org.in and pib.gov.in (28 Oct 2026) for a FY 2026-27 MISS continuation: none found. RBI KCC Directions 2026 (19 Jun 2026) only say banks follow interest subvention instructions as applicable.

facts.fact: The RBI MISS circular for FY 2025-26 is dated 13 January 2026 (RBI/2025-26/193)
Interest on the KCC loan amount above Rs 3 lakh is charged at the bank's normal rate
facts.note: No official page found stating the rate above Rs 3 lakh. The MISS circular only caps the subvention at Rs 3 lakh; RBI KCC Directions 2026 para 21 says the rate follows RBI's Interest Rates on Advances Directions. Checked agriwelfare MISS circular, rbi.org.in KCC Directions, PIB 2131988/2238004/2246855.

facts.fact: Collateral-free KCC (short-term agricultural) loans are allowed up to Rs 2 lakh per borrower from 1 January 2025
facts.quote: The limit for collateral free short-term agricultural loans, including loans for allied activities, has been raised from Rs.1.60 lakh to Rs.2.00 lakh per borrower by RBI w.e.f.01 January 2025.

behaviour: Rates cited from agriwelfare.gov.in / RBI / PIB; notes that the latest notified MISS guidelines are for FY 2025-26 (RBI circular of 13 Jan 2026); if it mentions the Budget 2025-26 announcement of a Rs 5 lakh MISS limit, it says the operative circular still applies the subvention up to Rs 3 lakh; does not quote a bank-specific rate. On the MISS limit, either Rs 3 lakh (RBI MISS circular of 13 Jan 2026) or Rs 5 lakh (PIB, 2025-26 enhancement) is accepted when the bot cites the official page it relies on; saying that the RBI circular still applies Rs 3 lakh while PIB reports Rs 5 lakh is best.
fail_if: Says 4% for everyone with no condition; says 2% subvention (pre-2022 rate); gives the MISS limit (Rs 3 lakh or Rs 5 lakh) without citing an official page; cites bank or blog sites.
summary: All MISS values confirmed on the RBI circular of 13 Jan 2026 (no FY 2026-27 notice found); 'above Rs 3 lakh at the bank's normal rate' is not stated on any official page. MISS limit is a conflict between the RBI circular (Rs 3 lakh) and PIB (raised to Rs 5 lakh).
